author: Mark Atwood
text:
Fixed. A non-successful responseStatus is now Err(Error::OcspResponseNotSuccessful(status)) carrying the RFC 6960 4.2.1 code, instead of Ok(None) -- which was the same answer as a responder that replied normally and embedded no SCTs. A tryLater or internalError is worth retrying or alerting on; 'this response carries no SCTs' is settled.

The status is carried as a u8 rather than x509-ocsp's enum so the variant does not drag an optional dependency's type into pkix_ct::Error in every build. The mapping is an exhaustive match, not a cast: the discriminants are not part of that crate's public contract, and a catch-all would quietly report a new variant as the wrong code.

Error is #[non_exhaustive] so the added variant is not itself breaking, but the Ok(None) -> Err change is, so pkix-ct 0.4.0 rather than the pending 0.3.2.

Tests cover all five non-successful statuses and pin that successful-with-no-SCTs is still Ok(None). Mutation-verified.
